description: Media Arts Year 3-4 width tiers — 5 standards, all capability strands. Generated from width_generation_prompt.md v1.0.
subject: Media Arts

width_notes.minimum_width: The narrowest single context that honestly meets the descriptor's command term — one production task, one media form, one context.
width_notes.typical_width: Full Y3-4 scope from common elaboration cases — multiple media production contexts engaged, ideas communicated with intentional use of media languages and technologies.
width_notes.wider: Additional task contexts: different genres or forms, different production approaches, collaborative publication contexts, First Nations media arts connections.
width_notes.elaborations: ACARA elaborations used as source data. First Nations elaborations always represented in wider.

AC9AMA4C01.minimum_width: Use media languages and at least one production process (e.g. photography, soundscape, or short film) to construct a representation that communicates ideas, perspectives or meaning — making deliberate decisions about at least one element (framing, sound, sequencing).
AC9AMA4C01.typical_width: Construct representations using multiple media technologies and production processes across forms (photography, soundscape, moving image, publication); apply shot types, angles, lighting and text to still or moving images; sequence visual and audio elements to communicate meaning without dialogue where appropriate; collaborate with others on a small publication.
wider: Create a short film that communicates connection to a place in the community — drawing on First Nations Australian media arts works about Country/Place for inspiration and using camera angles, lighting and sound to convey feeling without dialogue
Create a zine or small publication using collaged images, text and drawings to explore ideas significant in students' lives — using digital or analog tools and reflecting on audience response

Create a soundscape using Foley sounds and recorded sounds (found objects, voice, recording technology) to accompany a moving image — experimenting with volume, layering and voice to create a sense of environment
elaborations: taking a series of photographs that show themselves and their friends as comic superheroes and villains through setting, costume and body language

creating a soundscape to accompany a moving image that includes Foley sounds and recorded sounds on a variety of devices to explore volume, layering and the use of voice to create a sense of environment

using learning from explorations of media arts works that communicate First Nations Australians' connection to and responsibility for Country/Place to devise media arts works that communicate their own connection to and responsibility for place
experimenting with the camera and framing the subject, using shot types, angles and lighting, and experimenting to apply text to still or moving images, such as credits in a title sequence
filming a short sequence that focuses on conflict by selecting camera angles, lighting and/or costume to convey meaning without dialogue
collaborating with others to make a small publication to explore ideas that are significant in their lives; for example, a zine or new website, using collaged images and texts and drawings

AC9AMA4D01.minimum_width: Explore at least one media technology and use it to shape an idea — experimenting with how a change in the technology (sound effect, image edit, text addition) affects the meaning or mood of a story.
AC9AMA4D01.typical_width: Develop production skills across multiple media technologies and forms; experiment with suspense through colour, shot type and editing; create Foley sounds using available resources; use storyboarding as a planning tool; apply Viewpoints questions to refine production decisions; review, sort, delete and modify captured media elements.
wider: Investigate how conventions of a news story or video game communicate meaning — examining how speech bubble text, headlines, and framing choices reflect character voice and perspective; apply findings to original production work

Explore digital and analog storyboarding as a planning tool for a short film, stop motion or comic strip — rearranging boards to change narrative meaning and testing how different sequences affect an audience's response
Experiment with how sound effects change the meaning of images by creating multiple soundscapes for the same image sequence and comparing audience responses to each version
elaborations: experimenting with suspense to create meaning and sustain representations; for example, exploring the way colour, shot type and editing techniques are used to communicate film genre
investigating how the conventions of a news story or video game communicate meaning
exploring different ways of creating sounds when making a soundscape; for example, creating Foley sounds with available resources
exploring media technologies and languages when creating sound effects or images to convey a mood or main idea of a story
using Viewpoints to develop questions to respond to their experiences as they work, such as, "In what ways does the meaning of the image change when I manipulate the sound effects?"

AC9AMA4E01.minimum_width: Identify meaning in at least one media arts work from a different social, cultural or historical context — describing how the work communicates its ideas and for what purpose.
AC9AMA4E01.typical_width: Explore media arts works made across different social, cultural and historical contexts; compare works made for different purposes using appropriate language; identify conventions and features in a variety of media types; discuss representations, stereotypes and storytelling approaches in different contexts.
wider: Investigate how traditional First Nations Australian stories are being retold using media technologies — exploring animation, stop motion and green screen works and discussing how media arts concepts (framing, sound, editing) serve cultural storytelling purposes

Compare how the same type of event or story (e.g. a school excursion, a community celebration) is represented differently across different media types (news report, social media post, photo essay) — identifying how purpose and platform shape representation
Research representations of family or community in media arts works from different historical periods or countries — comparing how cultural values are visible in storytelling conventions
elaborations: sequencing images, sounds and/or text to clearly establish the beginning, middle and end of a story or event

identifying meaning and describing representations in media arts works from different social, cultural or historical contexts; for example, examining the different ways traditional stories are retold using media technologies or the use of stereotypes in advertising
comparing media arts works made for different purposes using appropriate language, and identifying features such as use of conventions in a variety of media types
using appropriate language to discuss the meaning of their own media arts works
investigating digital or analog storyboarding as a planning tool

AC9AMA4E02.minimum_width: Explore one media arts work created by First Nations Australians that communicates connection to and responsibility for Country/Place — identifying at least one way media languages (framing, sound, text, symbols) are used to convey this connection.
AC9AMA4E02.typical_width: Explore multiple First Nations Australian media arts works across forms; identify and describe how cultural expressions communicate connection to and responsibility for Country/Place (naming Country, acknowledging Ancestors, singing or speaking in language); investigate how screen-based storytelling maintains language and ways of life; collect and reflect on media arts works created for festivals or ceremonies.
wider: Explore an interactive map of First Nations Australian languages as a media arts work — investigating how media technologies and languages create a relationship between the work and its viewer, and discussing how digital tools are used to communicate the diversity of First Nations cultures

Investigate how First Nations Australian media artists use media arts to communicate cyclic knowledge about land, sea, sky and waterways — examining how these representations differ from non-Indigenous representations of the same phenomena

Explore First Nations Australian media arts works created for ceremonial or festival contexts — collecting and sharing information about the occasion, purpose and audience, and reflecting on how these works communicate important knowledge about Country/Place
elaborations: identifying meaning and describing representations in media arts works created and/or co-created by First Nations Australians, such as how traditional stories of First Nations Australians are being retold using media technologies
recognising, through media arts, how First Nations Australians' cultural expressions often contain and communicate connection to and responsibility for Country/Place

exploring First Nations Australians' use of media arts to express connection to and responsibility for Country/Place, such as communicating knowledge about the local seasons or using screen-based storytelling to maintain language and unique ways of life
exploring how First Nations Australians use media arts concepts to communicate their connection to and responsibility for Country/Place
collecting and sharing information about media arts works created and produced by First Nations Australians for occasions such as festivals or ceremonies
exploring how stories and ideas can communicate connection to and responsibility for Country/Place

exploring a media arts work that includes images, sound and/or text and communicates the diversity of First Nations Australians' cultures, such as an interactive map of First Nations Australian languages

AC9AMA4P01.minimum_width: Share a media arts work in an informal setting, acknowledging at least one responsible media practice (e.g. obtaining permission to photograph peers, crediting creators).
AC9AMA4P01.typical_width: Share media arts works in informal settings applying responsible media practices — creating credits, seeking and acknowledging permission for photographs, formatting publications using appropriate text conventions; consider audience relationships and media concepts (audience, relationships) when presenting.
wider: Create a title sequence with credits for a class screening — selecting appropriate fonts, colour and display timing to accompany a series of moving images; reflecting on how these choices affect the audience experience
Document a school excursion or event through photography, seeking permission from class members, and publish for the school intranet — practising the full permission and publication workflow
Format and lay out a front-page news story or print advertisement using available software — applying media concepts of audience and relationships to typography, image selection and layout decisions
elaborations: creating credits in a title sequence and selecting appropriate fonts, colour and length of display time to accompany screening of a series of moving images
seeking permission to take photos of class members; for example, documenting a school excursion for publication on the school intranet

considering media concepts, such as audience and relationships, when formatting and laying out a story, using available software and appropriate text conventions for a front-page news story or print advertisement
